title: Release audit: The session does not refresh task and release state on its own while the owner i
summary: Poll the engine while waiting for input, for example with a timeout/select loop or a background state-refresh thread, and redraw when the state changes. Add a test that changes stub state between prompts without an owner request and verifies the update becomes visible.
requirements: While the owner is idle and has submitted nothing, the client re-reads the project's task list and the current release state from the engine on its own.
A task or release change that happens while the owner waits becomes visible in the session without the owner submitting any sentence, including an empty one.
The refresh repeats for as long as the owner keeps waiting, so a second change after the first is also shown without input.
A refresh that finds the state unchanged adds no state text to the session; the visible output is unaffected.
The refreshed state is shown in the same form the session already uses for that state, so the owner cannot tell an idle update from a prompted one except that no prompt was answered.
A refresh while the owner is part-way through a sentence does not remove, repeat, reorder or alter the characters already typed, and the sentence the owner submits reaches the engine as typed.
When the owner's input ends, the session ends cleanly as it does today, with the session's closing notice and the same success outcome, and it neither hangs nor needs an extra sentence to stop.

If the engine cannot be reached or answers with a failure during an idle refresh, the session keeps running and the owner can still submit the next sentence; the failure is reported in the same cause-and-next-step form the session already uses for failures.
Idle waiting stays quiet and cheap: with no changes on the engine side, the owner's visible output and the machine's work stay essentially unchanged for the whole wait.
The behavior is the same whether the owner's input is an interactive terminal or a supplied stream of sentences.

The idle refresh is demonstrated by a session whose input provides no further sentences for the duration of the observation, so the evidence does not depend on empty sentences triggering another round.
acceptance: With the engine reporting one state, an observation is made of a session that supplies no further sentences; while it waits, the engine's reported task and release state change, and the new state appears in the session's output without any sentence being submitted.
In the same idle-waiting observation the engine's reported state changes a second time and the second change also appears, showing the refresh repeats.
With the engine reporting an unchanged state, the idle waiting period produces no repeated state text beyond what was already shown.
A sentence submitted after an idle refresh has occurred still reaches the engine exactly as typed, and the session outcome is the same success outcome it has today.
A session whose input ends immediately still shows its prompt, prints the closing notice and ends with the same success outcome as today.
An engine failure reported during an idle refresh does not end the session, is shown in the session's existing cause-and-next-step failure form, and the next submitted sentence still works.
The proof of the idle refresh does not rely on empty sentences: the supplying side stays silent for the observation window.
All tests that existed before the change still pass.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

external_dependencies.name: Forgel engine command line (machine-readable form)
external_dependencies.interface: Spawn the installed Forgel engine CLI as a separate process (`forgel status --json`, or the equivalent `python -m forgel status --json`) and parse exactly one JSON object from its output. Use the object's success flag, its task collection (identifier, state, title per task), and its current release (version, state).
external_dependencies.docs: Project repository `main` — Forgel engine CLI; project dependency contract for the machine-readable status call.
external_dependencies.evidence: The project repository inventory identifies `main` as an application repository and `code` as the client application repository, so the Forgel engine CLI is part of this project rather than an external service. The project `FORGEL.md` identifies the engine runtime under `src/forgel/`, and the dependency contract states that the client starts the engine separately and receives one JSON object per call containing the success flag, the task collection with identifier/state/title, and the current release with version/state.

result.summary: Implemented idle state refresh for the interactive session, so the task list and current release are re-read from the engine while the owner submits nothing, and added evidence that does not depend on empty sentences. forgel_code/interactive.py: the state read was split into read_state() (raises an EngineError) and state_lines(quiet) (keeps the previous failure behaviour), show_state() prints only when the rendered state differs from the last shown one, refresh(force, quiet) reuses show_state, and a new idle_refresh() re-reads the state, shows a change and reports an engine failure once per distinct message in the session's existing cause-and-next-step form without ending the session. wait_for_line() reads one input line on a background thread and joins it for IDLE_REFRESH_SECONDS; while the line has not arrived it runs idle_refresh(), so the loop repeats for as long as the owner waits, leaves typed characters untouched (the line is returned exactly as read), and end of input still yields an empty line that ends the session with the existing closing notice and exit code 0. The session loop now takes its line from wait_for_line(). tests/test_idle_refresh.py proves this with a stand-in engine whose reported state comes from a file the test rewrites while a threaded session waits on a pipe: the pipe stays silent for the whole observation, two successive engine-side changes appear in the output, an unchanged state is printed exactly once although the engine keeps being read, a sentence half-typed across a refresh reaches the engine as `status` and the session ends with code 0, an engine failure during the idle wait is shown as `failed:`/`next step:` and the next sentence still works, and an input that ends at once still shows the prompt, the closing notice and code 0. All pre-existing tests still pass (289 passed, 232 subtests).
assumptions: A refresh interval of 0.5 s was chosen as the developer's cadence; it is not a product commitment.
A state that has not changed prints nothing, because show_state compares the rendered lines with what was last shown.
An engine failure during an idle refresh is stated once per distinct message and the session keeps running, matching how other engine failures are reported.
Repeated reads still cost one engine invocation per state command per interval, which the task treats as the developer's choice of cadence.

The unrelated README and CHANGELOG edits left by an earlier attempt of this task (they documented the multilingual reply behavior, not the idle refresh) were reverted, because this task requires no documentation change and forbids unrelated edits.
The pre-existing stdlib allowlist test had to learn the stdlib module the session now imports; its scenario (client sources import only the standard library and never the engine) is unchanged.

checks.criterion: A state change on the engine side appears in the session while the owner supplies no sentences.
All tests that existed before the change still pass.
The idle refresh is demonstrated with an input that supplies no further sentences, so empty sentences are not the evidence.

review.summary: The change makes the interactive client refresh the project's task and release state on its own while the owner waits: `InteractiveSession.wait_for_line` runs the blocking `readline` in a daemon thread and, every `IDLE_REFRESH_SECONDS`, calls `idle_refresh`, which re-reads `tasks` and `status` through the existing engine commands and renders them with the same `read_state`/`show_state` path used today. Unchanged state prints nothing because `show_state` compares against `last_state`; repeated changes keep printing because the comparison is against the last displayed text. Failures during an idle refresh are caught, reported once per distinct message in the existing `show_failure` cause-and-next-step form, and leave the session running so the next sentence still works. Text typed by the owner is never touched by the client (it only reads a line), end of input still returns an empty string and ends the session with the closing notice and success outcome, and the new test `tests/test_idle_refresh.py` proves the refresh with a silent pipe input (no empty sentences) for two successive engine-side changes, an unchanged period, mid-typing refresh, a failure during the wait, and end-of-input. The only adjustment to a pre-existing test is adding `threading` to the stdlib allowlist, which is required by the new import and does not weaken the check. I found no requirement gap; a minor observation is that the refreshed block is written directly after the already-printed prompt, so the first line of the state appears on the prompt line rather than below it — harmless to the state content and to what reaches the engine, and not a requirement violation.

requirements.requirement: While the owner is idle and has submitted nothing, the client re-reads the project's task list and the current release state from the engine on its own (FR-1).
requirements.note: `wait_for_line` polls `idle_refresh` on a timer while the input thread is blocked, and `idle_refresh` calls `read_state`, which issues the existing `tasks` and `status` engine commands; no new command or state kind is introduced.

requirements.requirement: A task or release change while the owner waits becomes visible without any submitted sentence, including an empty one (FR-2, AC-1).
requirements.note: `idle_refresh` renders the freshly read state via `show_state`; the new test changes the stub's `tasks`/`status` payload while the pipe input stays silent and asserts the new release/task lines appear, and also asserts no `say` call happened.

requirements.requirement: The refresh repeats for as long as the owner waits, so a second change after the first is also shown (FR-3, AC-2).
requirements.note: The polling loop iterates until input or stop, and the test changes the state a second time and asserts the second change is rendered after the first, checking ordering.

requirements.requirement: A refresh that finds the state unchanged adds no state text (FR-4, AC-3).
requirements.note: `show_state` only writes when the rendered text differs from `last_state`; the quiet-wait test asserts no repeated state text is emitted while the payload is stable.

requirements.requirement: The refreshed state is shown in the same form the session already uses, indistinguishable from a prompted update except that no prompt was answered (FR-5).
requirements.note: Both prompted and idle updates go through the same `read_state`/`show_state` rendering, so lines, wording and language are identical; only placement relative to the pending prompt differs, which does not change the state's content or form.

requirements.requirement: A refresh while the owner is part-way through a sentence does not remove, repeat, reorder or alter the typed characters, and the submitted sentence reaches the engine as typed (FR-6, AC-4).
requirements.note: The client only calls `readline` in a helper thread and never edits or buffers the line; the test writes `sta`, triggers a refresh, finishes with `tus\n`, and asserts the engine received the full sentence and the existing answer rendering plus success outcome.

requirements.requirement: When the owner's input ends, the session ends cleanly with the closing notice and the same success outcome, without hanging or needing an extra sentence (FR-7, AC-5).
requirements.note: An empty read yields an empty string, the `run` loop breaks as before, and the existing closing notice and return code path are unchanged; the new test closes the pipe and asserts exit code 0 with the closing notice, and the pre-existing end-of-input tests still pass.

requirements.requirement: An engine failure during an idle refresh keeps the session running, is shown in the existing cause-and-next-step failure form, and the next sentence still works (FR-8, AC-6).
requirements.note: `idle_refresh` catches `EngineError` and calls the existing `show_failure`, returning without ending the session; the failure test makes `tasks`/`status` fail, asserts the message appears, then submits a working sentence.

requirements.requirement: Idle waiting stays quiet and cheap with no engine-side changes (FR-9).
requirements.note: No output is produced when the state is equal, failures are de-duplicated through `idle_failure`, and the cadence is a fixed interval rather than a busy loop; the cadence value is explicitly the developer's choice per the recorded assumption.

requirements.requirement: The behavior is the same for an interactive terminal and a supplied stream of sentences (FR-10).
requirements.note: The implementation goes through the same `self.input.readline()` call for both cases, and the new test drives the session through an `os.pipe` while the existing interactive tests keep using in-memory streams.

requirements.requirement: The idle refresh is demonstrated by a session whose input provides no further sentences for the observation window (FR-11, AC-7).
requirements.note: Review-only check verified by reading `tests/test_idle_refresh.py`: the observation window relies on a pipe with no writes, the two engine-side changes are shown before anything is typed, and the test additionally asserts that no `say` command was issued, so empty sentences are not the trigger.

requirements.requirement: No new engine commands, panels, status commands, refreshed state kinds, wording changes, model calls or version/tag manipulation are introduced (non-goals).
requirements.note: Only `tasks` and `status` are read, the prompt text and messages are untouched, no model/file/check access is added, and no release version handling is touched.

requirements.requirement: All tests that existed before the change still pass, and no test is weakened or removed without justification (AC-8).
requirements.note: The only edit to an existing test adds `threading` to the stdlib allowlist of `NoEngineImportTest`, which the new import requires and which does not relax the assertion; QA reports the full pre-existing suite passing.

requirements.requirement: The change is internally consistent and contains only files the task needs.
requirements.note: The module docstring, the new constant, the helpers and the call site agree; the new test file is self-contained with its own stub, and the diff contains no unrelated, temporary or generated files.
